front: Read one cell of a grid
back: grid[r][c] — row first, then column.

front: Number of rows and columns
back: rows = len(grid) · cols = len(grid[0])

front: Build an empty rows × cols grid safely
back:
[[0] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
Not [[0] * cols] * rows (one row shared).

front: Visit the neighbors of (r, c)
back: Bounds check before reading: grid[-1] silently reads the last row.

front: The 8 neighbors
back: The 4 straight moves plus the 4 diagonals.

front: Big-O of visiting every cell of an m × n grid
back: O(m · n). Two loops, but one visit per cell.

front: Transpose: where does (r, c) go?
back: To (c, r). An m × n grid becomes n × m.

front: Transpose in one line
back: [list(row) for row in zip(*grid)]

front: Main and anti-diagonal cells
back: Main: r == c. Anti: r + c == n − 1. One loop over i reads both.

front: Trigger: "no repeats in each row / column / box"
back: One set per group. Box index (r // 3) * 3 + c // 3.

front: Trigger: "rotate the image 90° in place"
back: Transpose, then reverse each row (clockwise).

front: Counterclockwise rotation in place
back: Transpose, then reverse the order of the rows.

front: Trigger: "spiral order"
back: Four walls (top, bottom, left, right) that shrink inward.

front: Spiral: which steps need a re-check, and why?
back: After two walls move, the rest may be one row, one column, or empty.

front: Turning-walker spiral: how do you turn right?
back: d = (d + 1) % 4 over [(0,1), (1,0), (0,-1), (-1,0)]. Turn when the next cell is outside or filled.

front: Trigger: "update in place, but each change depends on the original"
back: Record first, write second. Keep the record in spare cells or extra states, not a copy.

front: LC 36 Valid Sudoku — key idea
back:
• 27 sets: rows, cols, boxes
  • Skip "."
  • Return True only after every cell (M7)

front: LC 48 Rotate Image — key idea, trap
back:
• Transpose in place, swapping only c > r
  • Reverse each row
  • Trap: swapping every (r, c) undoes itself

front: LC 54 Spiral Matrix — key idea
back:
• Four walls; walk top, right, bottom, left
  • Re-check before bottom and left
  • Test 1 × n and n × 1 first

front: LC 59 Spiral Matrix II — key idea
back:
• Same walk, writing 1..n²
  • Or a turning walker with (d + 1) % 4

front: LC 73 Set Matrix Zeroes — why not zero immediately?
back: New zeros would trigger more zeroing. Record first, then write.

front: LC 73 Set Matrix Zeroes — O(1) space
back:
• Row 0 / column 0 hold the flags
  • Save first_row_zero, first_col_zero first
  • Zero row 0 and column 0 last

front: LC 289 Game of Life — the four states
back: Second pass: 2 → 0, 3 → 1.

front: LC 289 Game of Life — the rules
back:
• live, < 2 neighbors → dies
  • live, 2 or 3 → lives
  • live, > 3 → dies
  • dead, exactly 3 → lives

front: grid[c][r] instead of grid[r][c]
back: Reads the wrong cell, or crashes on a non-square grid. Row first. (M1 in a new form.)

front: Why must the bounds check come first?
back: Negative indexes don't crash in Python. grid[-1] reads the last row: a silent wrong answer.

front: Valid Sudoku: what's wrong with r // 3 + c // 3?
back: It gives 0–4, so different boxes share an index. Use (r // 3) * 3 + c // 3.

front: Set Matrix Zeroes O(1): why zero row 0 and column 0 last?
back: They hold the flags the inner cells still need.

front: New bug type (lab 4.09): missing re-check after walls move
back: The bottom row of a 1 × n grid is printed again backward. Check: "Is there still a row left?" (Candidate M10.)
